title: when someone asks what's the point of watching/making movies? what's your genuine answer?

commenti.body: Yeah but it isn’t though. I can be, but the “point@ of art isn’t just valid entertainment

Pointing out that in modern capitalist economies, art and culture are not valued whatsoever since they aren’t easily commodified. This has led to most people only engaging with art as entertainment, and if that’s ALL art is to you, it’s no longer art, since you need to engage with art. To be clear, I’m not saying art can’t be entertainment, but if you refuse to engage with art on any other level than vapid entertainment you use purely for escapism, then you’re not treating it like art, and art is born out of how humans create and then engage with a piece.

Due to all of this, the only easily commodified form of art is pure entertainment, and this has led to the incredibly misguided and ignorant view that it’s really just empty fun but nothing else, it serves no true purpose. This couldn’t be further from the truth

Humans are highly complex social animals with high complex inner lives and interpersonal relationships, yet sadly we can never see life through someone else eyes. This is a MASSIVE problem, because it leads to feelings of isolation and disorder among people and social groups. How was this problem fixed? Well, in the same way that science is the exploration of objective reality, art is the exploration of subjective reality. Language is useful but it’s an ultimately clumsy technology that’s incapable of fully translating complex inner experience to others. Art is our best tool to for this exact task. Various forms of art find ways to trigger primal emotional reactions that create not only a shared sense of empathy, but give you a window into the experiences of others. You know that “shit I thought I was the only person who felt this way, I guess im not so alone”. Or in the same way humans will mentally picture the future and plan so they can be prepared for the future, art takes you to this cerebral place that allows for the processing of emotions and shared sense of understanding and unity. Without art, our societies and cultures would have fallen apart a LONG time ago. 

Even in the most brutal periods of history, each and every culture deeply understood the importance of art and culture. Think about it, it I say “The Romans”, “the celts”, “the Greeks”, “ancient China”, “ancient India”. What’s the first image in your head? It’s there armour, clothing, architecture, beliefs, culture, gods, it’s there art and culture!!!! (All of these things involve art) 

Why do you think that whoever a fascistic goverment or movement rises up, the first thing they do is ban types of art, literature, movies etc? Because movies are not just “meant to be entertainment”. They can be, but they are such an incredibly powerful tool that we not only use to better understand ourselves and others, but to fast track emotional processing, planning, political movements etc etc

And even movies that are just meant to be entertaining, that shit can be so healthy for you, to help you destress! But it’s important we make sure we don’t only engage with art as entertainment, we need to be careful we don’t allow oppressive structures to take those things way with insidious tactics like cutting funding etc

Saying that "nothing will last" is an lazy way of trying to wallow in misery and self pity.  Plus, it doesn't really shed light on anything.  If "nothing lasts," then why do *anything,*  at all, not just making movies.  Why even try to prolong your life if "nothing lasts?"  Just lay down until you stop breathing.  


But that is boring.  Pulling yourself out of the misery-mud and trying to do things is just more fun.  So what if nothing lasts?  Do those things anyway.  Do them for yourself, and maybe someone else will come along and see them and enjoy them.  As long as you're still trying to do things, to make things, there is still hope of stumbling upon some unexpected moment of joy.  It won't last, but you will have it.  


And there is joy in creating something, in producing a thing that had not existed in this world before.  Even if it won't last, it was still here, and you will always know that it was.
Just stop reading philosophy. People watch movies, because they entertain you.
You're more likely to encounter someone who explains why they don't like watching movies, not the other way round.
This is like an AI generated para, which is a compliment compared to saying it's simply a few badly misunderstood concepts strung together.

It's entertainment and relaxation and enjoyment. Full stop.

It's also something to do on a date, something to take the kids or grandkids to on a rainy Saturday afternoon, something to talk about around the water cooler at the office.

The nihilistic view on how it matters? Phhhssst. If you're going to be nihilistic, be nihilistic all the way and ask what's the point of living when you're just going to die anyway.

As a filmmaker I just love to tell stories, either inspiring stories or something that is entertaining. The entire point is to either have fun or be entertained, alone or with friends/family at home or in theater or anywhere. 

Entertainment is one point, informative could be another. Whether it’s books, magazines, internet browsing, sports, art. I mean take the example of Picasso, was he wasting his time?

What the existentialists ultimately perceived was that while nothing is *intrinsically* meaningful, meaning is real and it is formed on human terms - through our own relationships, values, and language. 

Cinema is a language. Films can not only carry real meaning, but the form is a unique vehicle for new possible meanings. To deny yourself cinema on the grounds of nihilism would be equal to denying yourself words or even thought. 

To me cinema (as well as literature, theatre, poetry, some games) is a necessary language for modern thinkers to communicate nuanced truths about life and what it means to be human. It's meaningful in that it tells me something about myself and helps me empathise with others. So I'd never really be interested in discounting any cinematic experience on the grounds that it's meaningless. If anything can be meaningful, movies can.

It's spectator entertainment.  Those who ask you, do they watch sports, play video games, read books, anything like that? It's entertainment . If they are so good that they don't have any sedentary forms of entertainment,  good on them
It doesn't matter what it is. If you enjoy something then it's never a waste of time. Enjoyment is the point.
If there's no joy or money in it, then there is no reason. Applies to other things as well. I enjoy watching and making movies, so i do. Simple.
